80: 		posting_lists_its.emplace_back(std::move(pl));
81: 		const auto& it = posting_lists_its.back().it;

83: 		docid_base = std::min(docid_base, it->first);

85: 		++q_term_it;

91: /**
92: * Function responsible for the DAAT algorithm for query processing.
93: * @param query The query to be processed.
94: * @param conj If true, the query is processed in conjunctive mode.
95: * @param top_k The number of top results to be returned.
96: * @return A vector of results.
97: */
98: template<class LVT>
99: std::vector<result_t> Index<LVT>::query(std::set<std::string> query, bool conj, size_t top_k)
100: {
101: 	// Top-K results. This is a min queue (for that we use std::greater, of course), so that the minimum element can
102: 	// be popped
103: 	pending_results_t results;
104: 
105: 	auto [posting_lists_its, min_docid] = build_helpers(query, conj);
106: 	docid_t curr_docid = min_docid;
107: 
108: 	if(posting_lists_its.empty())
109: 		return {};
110: 
111: 	// Iterate all documents 'til we exhaust them
112: 	// O(|D| * |Q| * log(|K|))
113: 	while(not posting_lists_its.empty())
114: 	{
115: 		score_t score = 0;
116: 
117: 		bool contains_all_terms = std::all_of(posting_lists_its.begin(), posting_lists_its.end(),
118: 				[&curr_docid](const PostingListHelper& pl) {return pl.it->first == curr_docid;});
119: 
120: 		// Score current document
121: 		if(not conj or contains_all_terms)
122: 		{
123: 			for(auto& posting_helper : posting_lists_its)
124: 			{
125: 				const auto& [docid, freq] = *posting_helper.it;
126: 				if(docid != curr_docid)
127: 					continue;
128: 
129: 				score += posting_helper.pl.score(posting_helper.it, scorer);
130: 			}
131: 
132: 			// Push computed result in the results, only if our score is greater than worst scoring doc in results
133: 			if(results.size() < top_k or score > results.top().score)
134: 			{
135: 				results.push({curr_docid, score});
136: 
137: 				// If necessary pop-out the worst scoring element
138: 				if (results.size() > top_k)
139: 					results.pop();
140: 			}
141: 		}
142: 
143: 		docid_t next_docid = DOCID_MAX;
144: 		// Move iterators to current docid or (the next closest one)
145: 		for(auto posting_helper_it = posting_lists_its.begin(); posting_helper_it != posting_lists_its.end(); )
146: 		{
147: 			posting_helper_it->it.nextG(curr_docid);
148: 
149: 			// We exhausted this posting list, let's remove it
150: 			if(posting_helper_it->it == posting_helper_it->pl.end())
151: 			{
152: 				posting_helper_it = posting_lists_its.erase(posting_helper_it);
153: 				continue;
154: 			}
155: 
156: 			next_docid = std::min(next_docid, posting_helper_it->it->first);
157: 
158: 			// Continue
159: 			++posting_helper_it;
160: 		}
161: 		curr_docid = next_docid;
162: 	}
163: 
164: 	return convert_results(results, top_k);
165: }

13: /**
14:  * Represents a phrase literal consisting of one or more terms that must occur
15:  * in sequence.
16:  */
17: public class PhraseLiteral implements QueryComponent {
18: 	// The list of individual terms in the phrase.
19: 	private List<String> mTerms = new ArrayList<>();
20: 
21: 	// The kth position between two terms, k = 1 for phrase literals, k = n for NEAR
22: 	// /k literals where n is entered by user
23: 	private int k;
24: 
25: 	/**
26: 	 * Constructs a PhraseLiteral with the given individual phrase terms.
27: 	 */
28: 	public PhraseLiteral(List<String> terms, int k2) {
29: 		mTerms.addAll(terms);
30: 		k = k2;
31: 	}
32: 
33: 	/**
34: 	 * Constructs a PhraseLiteral given a string with one or more individual terms
35: 	 * separated by spaces.
36: 	 */
37: 	public PhraseLiteral(String terms, int k2) {
38: 		mTerms.addAll(Arrays.asList(terms.split(" ")));
39: 		k = k2;
40: 	}
41: 
42: 	/**
43: 	 * Constructs a PhraseLiteral given a string with one or more individual terms
44: 	 * separated by spaces.
45: 	 */
46: 	public PhraseLiteral(String terms) {
47: 		mTerms.addAll(Arrays.asList(terms.split(" ")));
48: 	}
49: 
50: 	@Override
51: 	public List<Posting> getPostings(Index index) {
52: 		// Retrieve the postings for the individual terms the phrase and positional merge them together.
53: 		List<Posting> result = null;
54: 
55: 		if (mTerms != null) {
56: 			try {
57: 				result = intersectPostings(mTerms, index);
58: 			} catch (Exception e) {
59: 				e.printStackTrace();
60: 			}
61: 		}
62: 		return result;
63: 	}
64: 
65: 	/**
66: 	 * The intersectPostings finds a list of postings that are common to two given terms and iterates over the
67: 	 * length of the phrase to find any point where there are no common postings, Finally it gives all the postings
68: 	 * where the whole phrase is present.
69: 	 * @param Terms 	string term or words in the phrase
70: 	 * @param index		index to query to get the postings
71: 	 * @return			list of posting where the whole phrase or near k operator exists
72: 	 */
73: 	public List<Posting> intersectPostings(List<String> Terms, Index index) {
74: 
75: 		List<Posting> common = new ArrayList<>();
76: 		int i = mTerms.size() - 1;
77: 		while (i > 0) {
78: 
79: 			String term1 = Terms.get(i);
80: 			String term2 = Terms.get(--i);
81: 			List<Posting> postingResult1 = index.getPostings(term1);
82: 			List<Posting> postingResult2 = index.getPostings(term2);
83: 
84: 			if (CollectionUtils.isEmpty(postingResult1) || CollectionUtils.isEmpty(postingResult2)) {
85: 				return Collections.EMPTY_LIST;
86: 			} else {
87: 				if (CollectionUtils.isEmpty(common))
88: 					common = positionalIntersect(postingResult1, postingResult2, k);
89: 				else
90: 					common = positionalIntersect(common, postingResult2, k);
91: 				if (common.isEmpty()) {
92: 					break;
93: 				}
94: 			}
95: 		}
96: 		return common;
97: 	}
98: 
99: 	/**
100: 	 * positionalIntersect checks how close to each other two terms in a given phrase are.
101: 	 * This method checks for both phrases and near K operators
102: 	 * @param term1 		The last term in a given phrase or remaining phrase
103: 	 * @param term2			The second last term in a given phrase or remaining phrase
104: 	 * @param k				The required distance between term1 and term2
105: 	 * @return				Positions where Term2..[k]..Term1 holds true for a given phrase or near K operator
106: 	 */
107: 	public List<Posting> positionalIntersect(List<Posting> term1, List<Posting> term2, int k) {
108: 		List<Posting> postingResult = new ArrayList<Posting>();
109: 		int i = 0, j = 0;
110: 		for (; i < term1.size() && j < term2.size();) {
111: 			if (term1.get(i).getDocumentId() == term2.get(j).getDocumentId()) {
112: 				List<Integer> pp1 = term1.get(i).getPositionsInDoc();
113: 				List<Integer> pp2 = term2.get(j).getPositionsInDoc();
114: 				List<Integer> phrasePosition = new ArrayList<Integer>();
115: 				for (Integer positions1 : pp1) {
116: 					for (Integer positions2 : pp2) {
117: 
118: 						/**
119: 						 * Term 1 and term 2 are moving from the end of the phrase to the beginning of the phrase.
120: 						 * Therefore, their arrangement is Term2.. [k].. Term1 in any given phrase.
121: 						 */
122: 
123: 						int relative_position = positions1 - positions2;
124: 						if ((relative_position <= k) && (relative_position >= 0)) {
125: 							phrasePosition.add(positions2);
126: 						} else if ((positions1 - positions2) > k) {
127: 							continue;
128: 						}
129: 					}
130: 				}
131: 				if (phrasePosition.isEmpty()) {
132: 					i += 1;
133: 					j += 1;
134: 					continue;
135: 				} else {
136: 					Posting ans = new Posting(term1.get(i).getDocumentId(), phrasePosition, 0);
137: 					postingResult.add(ans);
138: 					i += 1;
139: 					j += 1;
140: 					continue;
141: 				}
142: 			} else if (term1.get(i).getDocumentId() < term2.get(j).getDocumentId()) {
143: 				i += 1;
144: 			} else {
145: 				j += 1;
146: 			}
147: 		}
148: 		return postingResult;
149: 	}
150: 
151: 	@Override
152: 	public String toString() {
153: 		return "\"" + String.join(" ", mTerms) + "\"";
154: 	}
155: }
